newsitem.title: FINLAND: Metsa-Serla sees May-Dec loss, '96 profit.
newsitem.headline: Metsa-Serla sees May-Dec loss, '96 profit.

text.p: Finnish forest industry group Metsa-Serla Oy said in a statement on Tuesday it expected a loss in May-December but the full-year result would still be in the black.
"The result for the period January to April was a profit, after financial items, of 318 million markka. Present estimates indicate a loss for the period May to December," it said.
"Nevertheless, the group expects to make a profit for the current financial year," it said.
It cited a stronger than expected fall in prices of pulp and particularly paper products.
"The financial result will be affected by the greater than anticipated fall in market prices for pulp and, in particular, for paper," it said.
"The financial prospects for other business operations, including paperboard, tissue, packaging, containerboard and chemicals, are in line with the targets set for the year," it added.

Several development projects and investments this year to strengthen future competitiveness and market positions would result in non-recurring expenditure of around 300 million markka, Metsa-Serla said.

"The projects include the restructuring programme at MD Papier, establishment of the group's own paper and board marketing network, and the start-ups of Tako's rebuilt board machine, the new fine paper mill at Kirkinemi and the Metsa-Rauma pulp mill," it said.
Metsa-Serla said it would announce details of action to be taken to improve its competitiveness when it publishes its interim report for January-August on October 17.
